contentBody: **What is the primary purpose of segmentation?**
option.1: To create as many customer groups as possible
option.2: To divide a market into groups with meaningfully different needs or behaviours
option.3: To reduce the price of the product
answerExplanation: Segmentation splits a market into groups whose needs or behaviours actually differ.

contentBody: **Which is an example of behavioural segmentation?**
option.2: Customers living in Delhi and Mumbai
option.3: Customers who order food after 10 PM at least twice a week
option.4: Customers earning more than ₹10 lakh annually
answerExplanation: Behavioural segmentation uses what people do. Age, city, and income are demographic or geographic.

contentBody: **A company identifies four customer groups but decides to primarily serve working professionals. Which STP stage is this?**
answerExplanation: Choosing which of the groups to serve is targeting. Segmentation only creates the groups.

contentBody: **Which is the strongest example of a customer insight?**
option.3: Customers often get hungry around 4 PM but avoid regular snacks because they perceive them as unhealthy
answerExplanation: An insight states the situation and the reason. Age, city, and device ownership do not.

contentBody: **Which statement best describes a Point of Difference?**
option.1: A feature every competitor must offer
option.2: Something that matters to customers and helps distinguish the brand
option.4: A demographic characteristic of the audience
answerExplanation: A point of difference is what helps the customer choose this brand. A feature everyone must offer is a point of parity.
